```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(shinydashboard)
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)

```


```{r}

## Define UI ##
ui_1 <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "Very Creative Title Here"),  # Optional title
  
  dashboardSidebar(  # Sidebar with tabs
    sidebarMenu(
      menuItem("Visual 1", tabName = "Visual 1", icon = icon("chart-bar")),
      menuItem("Visual 2", tabName = "Visual 2", icon = icon("chart-bar"))
    )
  ),
  
    dashboardBody(  # Main body content
    tabItems(
      # First tab content
      tabItem(tabName = "Visual 1",
        fluidRow(
          box(
            title = "Average Response Time by Borough",
            plotOutput("complaintPlot", height = 500),
            width = 12  # Ensure the box takes full width
          )
        ),
        
        fluidRow(
          box(
            title = "Controls",
            selectInput("borough", "Select Borough:",
                        choices = unique(data_1$Borough),
                        selected = "Manhattan",
                        multiple = TRUE),
            selectInput("complaint", "Select Complaint Type:", 
                        choices = c("All Complaints", unique(data_1$`Complaint Type`)), 
                        selected = "All Complaints",
                        multiple = TRUE),
            sliderInput("dateRange", "Select Date Range:", 
                        min = min(data_1$`Created Date`, na.rm = TRUE), 
                        max = max(data_1$`Created Date`, na.rm = TRUE), 
                        value = c(min(data_1$`Created Date`, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                  max(data_1$`Created Date`, na.rm = TRUE))),
            width = 4  # Set width for the control panel
          )
        )
      ),
      
      # Second tab content
      tabItem(tabName = "Visual 2",
        h2("Average Response Time by Borough"),
        DTOutput("dataTavle")
      )
    )
  )
)
```


```{r}
## Define Server ##
server_1 <- function(input, output) {
  data_1 <- read.csv("data_1.csv")
  print(colnames(data_1))
  set.seed(122)
  histdata <- rnorm(500)
  
    # Reactive dataset based on user selections from controls
  filtered_data <- reactive({
    data_1 %>%
      filter(Borough %in% input$borough,
             `Complaint Type` %in% input$complaint | "All Complaints" %in% input$complaint,
             !is.na(Duration),  # remove rows with NA in Duration
             !is.na(`Created Date`),  # remove rows with NA in Created Date
             `Created Date` >= input$dateRange[1] & 
             `Created Date` <= input$dateRange[2]) %>%
      mutate(Duration = as.numeric(Duration))  # Ensure Duration is numeric
  })
  
  # Aggregated data for plotting
  aggregated_data <- reactive({
    filtered_data() %>%
      group_by(Borough) %>%
      summarise(Average_Duration = mean(Duration, na.rm = TRUE))  # Calculate average of Duration for each borough
  })
  
  # Render the plot with Plotly
  output$complaintPlot <- renderPlotly({
    data <- aggregated_data()  # Store the aggregated data
    
    # Create the Plotly bar plot
    ggplotly(
      ggplot(data, aes(x = Borough, y = Average_Duration, fill = Borough)) +
        geom_bar(stat = "identity") +  # Use "identity" to plot pre-aggregated data
        labs(title = "Average Response Time by Borough", 
             y = "Average Duration (Days)", 
             x = "Borough") +
        scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1))
    )
  })

  # Render the data table
  output$dataTable <- renderDT({
    aggregated_data()  # Display the filtered data based on user input
  })
  
}

```


```{r}
shinyApp(ui_1, server_1)
```
